Given the data set: 19, 10, 12, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, m, n. The mean and median of this data set are both 14. Which of the following statements must be true?
I. m \ge 14
II. n \le 16
III. m + n = 30

Choices: A) only I and II; B) only I and III; C) only II and III; D) I, II and III.
reasoning: The sum of the 11 numbers must be 14\times 11 = 154. The sum of the nine known numbers is 124, so m + n = 30, giving statement III. For the median to be 14 with an odd number of observations, exactly five values must be less than 14. The existing numbers less than 14 are 10,12,12,13,13 — already five. Therefore neither m nor n can be less than 14; otherwise the count of numbers <14 would exceed five and the median would shift below 14. Hence m \ge 14 and n \ge 14. Since m + n = 30 and both are \ge 14, the largest possible value for either is 16 (when the other is 14). Thus n \le 16 and m \le 16 also hold. All three statements are necessarily true, so the correct choice is D.
